title: lazy-sunday vietnamese bun cha
description: a winey, shattering combination of flavors and textures, featuring amazake and katsuramuki-cut pork. perfect for a lazy sunday afternoon.
instructions: in a small saucepan, combine 1/2 cup of amazake and 2 tablespoons of fish sauce. bring to a simmer over medium heat.
season the pork with salt, pepper, and 2 cloves of minced garlic.
bake the pork for 30 minutes, or until it reaches an internal temperature of 160f (71c).
while the pork is cooking, prepare the pickled carrots and daikon.
in a small bowl, whisk together 1/4 cup of rice vinegar, 2 tablespoons of sugar, and 1 tablespoon of grated ginger.
slice the carrots and daikon into thin strips and soak them in the pickling liquid for at least 30 minutes.
after the pork has cooked for 20 minutes, brush it with the amazake glaze and continue to bake for an additional 10 minutes.
once the pork is cooked, let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing it thinly against the grain.
assemble the bun cha by placing a few slices of the pork onto a plate, followed by a few strips of pickled carrots and daikon, and finishing with a sprinkle of fresh cilantro.
serve with a side of steamed rice or noodles for added depth of flavor.
